standard.title: Develop and Modify Inquiry Questions
standard.description: develop and modify questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y8 AC9HE8S01 (direct predecessor): develop questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue. Students can develop questions at Y8 level. Y9 adds two moves: (1) modifying questions to improve focus, and (2) operating with more complex, contemporary issues involving global markets, interdependence and globalisation. The 'modify' move is new and requires meta-cognitive reflection on question quality.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop and modify questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue.

nodes.label: Developing questions for complex economic issues
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop questions to investigate a complex contemporary economic and business issue, using economic and business concepts and terms.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least two questions using economic and business concepts that could guide an investigation of a named contemporary issue.
nodes.typical_width: Develop questions that investigate a complex contemporary economic and business issue — using the elaboration examples as models (e.g. 'How do participants in the global economy interact?', 'Why does international trade benefit Australian society?', 'How do businesses create and maintain a competitive advantage?'). Questions should be framed using relevant economic and business concepts and terms (interdependence, trade, competitive advantage, globalisation), be investigable (answerable through research), and be appropriately scoped for the issue's complexity.
wider: Develop questions for a multi-stakeholder issue (e.g. a trade dispute affecting Australian businesses, workers and consumers simultaneously) and explain what makes each question investigable
Develop questions that span multiple scales of analysis (local, national, global) for the same economic issue, and explain how the scale changes what evidence would be needed
Develop questions for a First Nations economic and business context (e.g. land rights and resource royalties, cultural IP and global markets) using appropriate terminology
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot frame questions at the right scope — specific enough to be investigable, broad enough to address the issue's complexity — will not be able to conduct meaningful inquiry. Poor questions at this stage mean all subsequent research, analysis and communication work is anchored to an inadequate inquiry frame.

response_modes.reason: Question quality requires explicit criteria: Is it investigable? Does it use appropriate concepts? Is it scoped to the issue's complexity? Teaching students to evaluate their own questions against criteria before committing to an investigation frame addresses the cascade risk.

success_criteria: Develops at least two questions that use economic and business concepts or terms
Questions are investigable — they can be answered through research into economic and business data or information
Questions address the complexity of a contemporary economic or business issue

nodes.label: Modifying questions to improve focus
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the focus and scope of an inquiry question and modify it to improve its usefulness for investigating an economic or business issue.
nodes.minimum_width: Take an existing inquiry question and modify it to improve its focus — explaining what was weak about the original and how the modification improves it.
nodes.typical_width: Develop and modify questions to improve the focus of an investigation using economic and business concepts and terms. Apply the elaboration examples as models: narrowing a broad question ('How can consumers protect themselves from risk?' → 'What strategies do Australian consumers use to manage scam risk?'), improving terminology precision, adjusting scope to match available evidence, and checking that modified questions genuinely advance the investigation rather than introducing a new tangent.
wider: Practise question modification through a structured peer feedback cycle — develop a question, receive structured critique on its focus and concept use, modify and re-evaluate
Apply modification to questions across different issue types (trade, consumer protection, competitive advantage) to develop transferable question-quality judgement
Evaluate a set of provided questions of varying quality for the same economic issue and rank them with justification — explaining what makes the best question better than the weaker ones

response_modes.reason: The modification move requires repeated practice with explicit feedback before it becomes reliable. Students tend to 'modify' by making questions longer rather than sharper. Practise-and-refine cycles with explicit criteria build the precision needed.

Practising modification across different economic issue contexts — trade, consumer risk, competitive advantage — builds transferable question-quality judgement rather than issue-specific question templates.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The modification move, practised across multiple economic contexts and through peer feedback, builds meta-cognitive inquiry skills that transfer to all Y9 economics investigations and to cross-disciplinary inquiry tasks.
success_criteria: Modifies at least one inquiry question and explains what was improved by the modification
The modified question is more focused, better scoped, or uses more precise economic terminology than the original
The modification does not introduce a new tangent — it sharpens the original question's focus
